Cowboy Core may be having a moment on fashion feeds, but in Sonoma County, the trend has considerably deeper roots. Ranching, horseback riding, Western wear and country music have long been part of the region’s culture. Now they’re becoming part of the travel experience, too.

In Windsor, Spur Saloon has opened as a country-western bar and live music venue with dancing, line dancing and karaoke. Grapevine Dance is bringing country line-dancing lessons to venues around the county, including the historic Washoe House and Twin Oaks Roadhouse. At Lake Sonoma, The Ranch at Lake Sonoma offers guided horseback rides through the 17,000-acre recreation area, with routes overlooking the lake, Dry Creek Valley and Rockpile wine region, including experiences that pair a ride with a picnic and local wine or beer.

The look can come home with you, too. Santa Rosa’s The Hattery is a working hat factory, showroom and museum specializing in Western hats and bespoke designs, while Blanton’s Boot & Hat in downtown Petaluma offers premium cowboy boots, custom hats, leather goods and Western apparel. On Sonoma Plaza, Large Leather has been crafting fine leather goods for more than 45 years, including belts with Western-style buckles, while Bosworth & Son General Merchandise in Geyserville has been selling Western wear since 1911. The historic mercantile remains a multigenerational family business and offers custom hat shaping, cleaning and restoration.

The Curated Take: This is where a social trend meets an authentic sense of place. Sonoma County doesn’t have to manufacture a cowboy aesthetic for visitors. It already has the ranches, horses, craftsmen, historic mercantiles and country music to support it. For travelers, that means Cowboy Core can be more than a pair of boots for the weekend. It can become a way of experiencing the region.

Photo credit: The Hattery

Four New Ways to Experience Sonoma County Beyond the Tasting Room https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/four-new-ways-to-experience-sonoma https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/four-new-ways-to-experience-sonoma Sandra Thomas-Comenole Mon, 07 Sep 2026 08:36:22 GMT

Wine may remain central to Sonoma County’s identity, but some of the destination’s newest experiences are looking elsewhere, toward food, agriculture, art and the redwoods.

In downtown Petaluma, Taste Petaluma brings four local concepts together under one roof: Barber Cellars, Petaluma Cheese Shop, Barber Lee Spirits and Nightcap Dessert Bar. Guests can move from Sonoma County wines and craft cocktails to artisan cheeses, chocolates and desserts in a relaxed lounge setting. In Santa Rosa, Gold Ridge Organic Farms is opening Heritage Apple Press, a 20,000-square-foot facility designed to process fruit from small and family-owned farms, helping preserve the region’s apple-growing heritage while supporting fresh-packed apples, juice, cider and vinegar.

Art is also becoming part of the resort experience. Fairmont Sonoma Mission Inn & Spa has debuted the Lori Austin Gallery at the Fairmont, a rotating pop-up gallery showcasing contemporary work by regional artists. And for travelers who would rather head into the trees, Sonoma Zipline Adventures is expanding with Redwood Aerial Adventure, a 40,000-square-foot ropes and challenge course expected to open in spring 2027, with aerial routes, sky bridges and a separate treetop play area for younger visitors.

The Curated Take: The appeal here is variety. Sonoma County can still be a wine destination, but travelers increasingly want something to do between tastings, whether that means discovering local producers, seeing regional art or climbing into a redwood canopy. These experiences give visitors more reasons to slow down and engage with the place itself.

Six New Restaurants Are Giving Sonoma County Even More Reasons to Stay for Dinner https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/six-new-restaurants-are-giving-sonoma https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/six-new-restaurants-are-giving-sonoma Sandra Thomas-Comenole Mon, 07 Sep 2026 08:31:07 GMT

Sonoma County’s culinary scene is having another busy season, with new restaurants and cafés adding everything from charcoal-grilled Northern California cooking to handmade pasta, East Coast bagels and Chinese-inspired food.

On Sonoma Plaza, the team behind the girl & the fig has opened Dead Letter in a historic former post office, where seasonal seafood, meats and vegetables share the menu with a globally minded wine list and postal-inspired cocktails. In Santa Rosa, Capriciano Osteria brings chef-owner Baki Bekci’s fine-dining background to a neighborhood-style Italian restaurant centered on handmade pasta, wood-fired pizza and Sonoma County ingredients. Meanwhile, Mei Mei is planned for Healdsburg, giving Sean Quan and Jenny Phan, the team behind Bazaar Sonoma, a new home for their Chinese-style food hall and grocery concept after their Forestville restaurant was lost in a 2025 fire.

West Sonoma County is also getting a new community gathering place with Graton Station, a café and bakery taking over the town’s former firehouse. In Sebastopol, Bonnie Bagels & Co. is bringing kettle-boiled, East Coast-style bagels to downtown, while Dolce Rosa Café in Santa Rosa’s Rincon Valley combines brunch, Italian-inspired dishes and specialty espresso drinks, with pistachio making an especially prominent appearance across the menu.

The Curated Take: The most interesting thing about Sonoma’s restaurant boom isn’t simply the number of openings. It’s the range of stories behind them. Chefs are bringing fine-dining experience into neighborhood spaces, couples are rebuilding after loss, historic buildings are finding new lives and longtime local businesses are creating gathering places. The result is a food scene that feels increasingly woven into the communities travelers come to explore.

Vietnam’s Flavours Take Cocktail Form at Four Seasons The Nam Hai https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/vietnams-flavours-take-cocktail-form https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/vietnams-flavours-take-cocktail-form Sandra Thomas-Comenole Mon, 07 Sep 2026 07:50:18 GMT

At Four Seasons Resort The Nam Hai in Hoi An, Vietnam’s culinary traditions are moving behind the bar for two nights this September. On September 12 and 13, 2026, Sol & Sao will host The Enigma Mansion, recognized by Asia’s 50 Best Bars, for an exclusive cocktail experience exploring the country’s regional ingredients, seasonal harvests and evolving mixology scene.

Under the theme “Two Cities, One Night,” the four-cocktail menu reinterprets familiar Vietnamese flavours through contemporary techniques. Strawberry combines whisky with strawberry whey, koji water, cacao wine and salted apricot; wintermelon pairs gin with cucumber, dill, pear, tonic and mezcal; beetroot brings together whisky, jasmine, Parmesan and tamarind; and a rice-inspired serve combines bourbon, red rice, butter, apple, miso vermouth and passionfruit seed bitters. The experience runs from 6:30 to 10:30 p.m., offering resort guests an opportunity to discover a different side of Vietnam’s culinary culture without leaving the property.

The Curated Take: The most interesting luxury hotel experiences increasingly go beyond simply showcasing local ingredients. They give travelers a new way to understand them. Here, Vietnamese flavours that might be encountered in a market or kitchen are transformed through modern mixology, connecting regional culinary heritage with the country’s contemporary food and beverage scene. It is a small but compelling example of how a resort can make a destination feel more discoverable, even from behind its own bar.

Photo credit: Four Seasons Resort The Nam Hai, Hoi An

Luang Prabang Glows for One Night Each Year at the Festival of Light https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/luang-prabang-glows-for-one-night https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/luang-prabang-glows-for-one-night Sandra Thomas-Comenole Mon, 07 Sep 2026 07:47:30 GMT

Once a year, on the October full moon, Luang Prabang transforms into a city of candlelight for Boun Lai Heua Fai, the Festival of Light. On October 26, 2026, illuminated boats made from bamboo and paper will wind through the UNESCO-listed old town to the sound of drums before being released onto the Mekong River. Temple grounds glow with lotus-shaped lanterns, while thousands of small krathong drift downstream carrying wishes into the current, marking the end of Buddhist Lent.

For travelers who want to experience the festival from a more intimate base, La Résidence Phou Vao, a Luxury Collection Resort & Spa, has created a Festival of Light Offer built around the celebration. A dedicated Guest Experience Curator can arrange guided access to the parade, lanterns and river, while the package includes daily breakfast, airport or railway transfers, old-town shuttle service, a $50 resort credit, daily sunset drinks and canapés, complimentary laundry and, for stays of three nights or more, a three-course dinner for two. The offer is available for bookings through October 31, 2026, with rates available upon request.

The Curated Take: Some cultural celebrations are best experienced as an event; others are best understood as a moment in the life of a place. Boun Lai Heua Fai is the latter. The combination of Buddhist tradition, candlelit temples, handmade lanterns and the Mekong at night offers a rare glimpse of Luang Prabang when its famously tranquil atmosphere takes on an entirely different rhythm. For travelers drawn to meaningful cultural experiences, timing a visit around the October full moon turns a stay in Luang Prabang into something considerably more memorable than a sightseeing stop.

Photo credit: La Résidence Phou Vao, a Luxury Collection Resort & Spa, Luang Prabang

Marc Garcia Inducted Into Arizona Tourism Hall of Fame https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/marc-garcia-inducted-into-arizona https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/marc-garcia-inducted-into-arizona Sandra Thomas-Comenole Mon, 07 Sep 2026 06:55:27 GMT

After nearly three decades shaping Arizona’s visitor economy, Visit Mesa President and CEO Marc Garcia has been inducted into the Arizona Tourism Hall of Fame, recognizing his sustained leadership in tourism and his role in positioning Mesa as a nationally recognized destination.

The honor was presented during the Governor’s Tourism Awards at the 2026 Arizona Governor’s Conference on Tourism in Tucson. Garcia joined Visit Mesa as president and CEO in 2012, and during his tenure, booked room nights and related visitor spending have increased by more than 891%, while the organization’s operating budget has grown by more than 300%. His work has extended beyond destination marketing, including statewide tourism advocacy and efforts to expand accessible travel. In 2019, Garcia led Mesa’s initiative to become the nation’s first Autism Certified City, an effort that has since trained thousands of hospitality employees, city personnel and community members in autism awareness.

Garcia’s career also includes 15 years with Visit Phoenix, where he worked on major tourism and convention initiatives and helped lead efforts to rebuild Arizona’s reputation as a welcoming destination following the 2010 passage of SB 1070. At the same Governor’s Tourism Awards, Visit Mesa’s Ashley Stwertnik, producer and host of the City Limitless podcast, received a Rising Star Award for her work telling Mesa’s story through multimedia and destination storytelling.

The Curated Take: Tourism leadership is often measured in hotel nights and visitor spending, but Garcia’s career illustrates the broader influence destination organizations can have on how a place is experienced. His work in accessible travel is particularly notable, demonstrating how destination marketing can extend into the design of a more welcoming visitor experience. The dual recognition for Garcia and Stwertnik also highlights something increasingly important in destination promotion: the people telling a place’s story can be just as influential as the campaigns themselves.

Photo credit: Visit Mesa

Sonoma County’s Culinary Scene Reaches New Heights With Three Michelin Stars for Enclos https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/sonoma-countys-culinary-scene-reaches https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/sonoma-countys-culinary-scene-reaches Sandra Thomas-Comenole Sun, 06 Sep 2026 18:09:04 GMT

Sonoma County has added another major distinction to its culinary reputation. Enclos Sonoma has risen from two Michelin stars to three in the 2026 Michelin Guide, placing the restaurant among the guide’s highest-rated destinations only months after making its debut with two stars in 2025.

The latest awards also brought a first Michelin star to Troubadour, while SingleThread retained its three-star designation and Green Star for its environmental sustainability and stewardship. Cyrus maintained its one-star rating. Beyond the starred restaurants, six Sonoma County establishments earned Bib Gourmand recognition for high-quality cooking at more accessible prices: El Molino Central, Valley Bar + Bottle, Glen Ellen Star, Khom Loi, Ramen Gaijin and Stockhome.

The Curated Take: Three Michelin stars is news anywhere, but Enclos’ trajectory makes the recognition particularly striking. Sonoma County’s culinary reputation is no longer simply an extension of its wine culture. The county has developed a dining ecosystem capable of supporting everything from highly ambitious tasting menus to neighborhood restaurants recognized for value, giving travelers another reason to plan an entire trip around the table.

Sonoma’s Wine Country Is Changing the Way Travelers Taste https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/sonomas-wine-country-is-changing https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/sonomas-wine-country-is-changing Sandra Thomas-Comenole Sun, 06 Sep 2026 14:35:11 GMT

Wine tasting in Sonoma County is becoming less about standing at a tasting bar and more about experiencing the landscape, history and people behind the bottle.

Marimar Estate Vineyards & Winery is celebrating its 40th anniversary in Sonoma County this year, marking four decades since Marimar Torres planted Chardonnay at Don Miguel Vineyard in the Green Valley of the Russian River Valley. Today, the family-owned estate farms 70 acres across the Russian River Valley and West Sonoma Coast, producing cool-climate wines including Chardonnay and Pinot Noir while continuing its focus on sustainability and multigenerational stewardship.

Elsewhere, Stone Edge Farm Estate Vineyards & Winery has opened La Maison, its first public tasting room after more than two decades of producing limited-production estate wines. The appointment-only experience brings together Moon Mountain District wines, regenerative agriculture, gardens and residential-style hospitality. The relationship extends to nearby Enclos, Chef Brian Limoges’ newly three-Michelin-starred restaurant, with an Enclos Lounge experience pairing Stone Edge Farm wines with small plates. At the Russian River estuary, Siren’s Cellar offers another distinctly different experience: a relaxed coastal wine bar overseen by sommelier and Monte Rio Cellars winemaker Patrick Cappiello, featuring natural wines, small producers and regional food.

The Curated Take: Sonoma’s newest wine experiences are increasingly about context. A bottle becomes more memorable when you understand the vineyard, the farm, the coastline or the chef connected to it. That shift makes Wine Country feel less like a series of tasting appointments and more like a destination where agriculture, hospitality and cuisine are part of the same story.

Sonoma County Makes Getting There Easier, From Austin and Denver to the Airport Parking Lot https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/sonoma-county-makes-getting-there https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/sonoma-county-makes-getting-there Sandra Thomas-Comenole Sun, 06 Sep 2026 14:25:57 GMT

Sonoma County is making the journey into Wine Country a little easier. Southwest Airlines will launch seasonal Saturday nonstop service between Charles M. Schulz Sonoma County Airport and Austin-Bergstrom International Airport on October 3, 2026, giving Central Texas travelers a direct route to Sonoma’s vineyards, redwood forests, Sonoma Coast and small towns.

The airline is also expanding its Denver service, moving to daily nonstop flights beginning March 11, 2027, after ramping up service during the fall, Thanksgiving and winter holiday periods. Meanwhile, travelers arriving at the airport will find a decidedly more modern experience on the ground. Charles M. Schulz Sonoma County Airport has introduced California’s first Metropolis drive-in, drive-out airport parking system, allowing registered travelers to enter and exit without tickets or payment kiosks. Vehicle recognition handles payment automatically, with digital receipts sent after the trip.

The Curated Take: Air access rarely feels like a travel story until it changes the way a destination can be reached. Sonoma County’s expanding connections to Austin and Denver do exactly that, opening the region to new drive-free itineraries while making the airport experience itself more seamless. For travelers accustomed to flying into larger Bay Area airports and driving north, STS increasingly makes the case for starting the Wine Country experience closer to the vineyards.

Island Hopper Brings Songwriters to the Water for 10 Days of Music https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/island-hopper-brings-songwriters https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/island-hopper-brings-songwriters Sandra Thomas-Comenole Sun, 06 Sep 2026 14:19:30 GMT

Southwest Florida’s Island Hopper Songwriter Fest returns September 18–27 with 10 days of intimate performances across Captiva Island, Cape Coral, downtown Fort Myers and Fort Myers Beach. Now in its 12th year, the festival brings more than 80 performances from acclaimed singer-songwriters to a distinctly tropical setting, with most shows free to attend. For those looking for a closer connection to the music, a limited selection of ticketed experiences pairs live performances with some decidedly memorable Southwest Florida settings.

This year’s special events include “Stars on the River,” featuring LOCASH and Alexandra Kay at Caloosa Sound Amphitheater; a Sunday brunch on Captiva with Dylan Altman and Tim James; Edwin McCain’s Westin Unplugged performance in Cape Coral; songwriter dinners in Cape Coral and downtown Fort Myers; and a sunset songwriter cruise departing Fort Myers Beach. The festival closes September 27 with Michael Ray performing a pool-party finale at Pink Shell Beach Resort & Marina, giving music lovers plenty of ways to build an entire getaway around the festival.

The Curated Take:
The best music festivals don’t simply give you a lineup; they give you a sense of place. Island Hopper does exactly that, turning beaches, waterways, restaurants, resorts and historic venues into part of the experience. A sunset cruise with a songwriter or live music overlooking the Gulf feels very different from sitting in a conventional concert hall, and that combination of intimate performances and tropical scenery makes this one worth planning a trip around.

Photo credit: Fort Myers – Islands, Beaches and Neighborhoods / Island Hopper Songwriter Fest
